findings.title: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow is documented for per-user access
findings.detail: Linear recommends OAuth2 for applications built for others to use. The flow redirects users to the authorize endpoint with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and scope, then exchanges the code at the token endpoint. Each connected person authorizes separately, so the access token is tied to that user's account.

findings.title: Use the default read scope for reading issue titles
findings.detail: The read scope gives read access for the user's account and is always present by default. It is the least-privilege documented grant that covers reading issues through the GraphQL API. Write scopes such as issues:create or write are not needed for the confirmed read-only use.

steps.title: Read the first page of issue titles
steps.detail: Send a GraphQL query to Linear's endpoint using the Bearer access token returned for the connected test user. The query requests the first 10 issues with title and pageInfo. A successful response has a data.issues object with edges, cursor values and pageInfo.hasNextPage and endCursor. Archived issues are excluded by default. This is a read-only query with no mutation.
steps.doneWhen: The response is HTTP 200 with no errors array, data.issues.edges contains issue node id and title values, and data.issues.pageInfo provides hasNextPage and endCursor for the next request. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: --data '{ "query": "{ issues { nodes { id title } } }" }' \

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: returned by the token exchange for the test user
